jurisdiction: South Africa — FIC Act 38 of 2001, Directive 9 (crypto-asset Travel Rule); FATF (2020) Virtual Asset Red Flag Indicators; FATF Recommendations 15 & 16; UNSC TFS (s.26A-26C)
source_notes: Drift Sentinel rulebook — professional draft schema (Rule ID, risk category, rule text, trigger, source, rule type, ATLAS mapping, capability primitives). DS-01..21 transcribed from the Drift Sentinel Twenty Example Rules DRAFT (09.2026). DS-22..40 extend the FATF (2020) red-flag indicator set and Directive 9 obligation themes to reach a 40-rule reference rulebook. All rule text is paraphrased for schema demonstration; verify exact wording against source before production use. Demonstration data only.

rules.name: Rapid deposit followed by rapid trade or withdrawal
rules.text: A large initial deposit is made to open a new account, inconsistent with the customer's declared profile, and the customer trades or withdraws most or all of the balance within a day or two of account opening.
rules.trigger: New account; deposit value inconsistent with stated profile; rapid trade/withdrawal (same day or next day).

rules.name: Structuring into sub-threshold transfers
rules.text: Transfers are structured into amounts just under record-keeping or reporting thresholds, or multiple high-value transfers are made in quick succession (e.g. within a 24-hour period).
rules.trigger: Repeated sub-threshold transfers, or high-value transfers clustered in a short time window.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.5, 'Size and frequency of transactions'

rules.name: Travel Rule — transmission of originator and beneficiary information
rules.text: An ordering CASP must transmit the originator's and beneficiary's required identifying information to the recipient CASP prior to or simultaneously with the transfer and may not execute the transfer if it cannot meet this requirement.
rules.trigger: Any qualifying crypto asset transfer between ordering and recipient CASPs.

rules.name: Transactions with counterparties with weak or absent KYC controls
rules.text: Funds are sent to, or received from, a VASP with weak or absent KYC/AML controls; separately, transfers involving an unhosted wallet must be subject to the CASP's own risk-based policy.
rules.trigger: Counterparty VASP has demonstrably weak/no CDD; or transfer involves an unhosted wallet.
rules.source: FATF (2020) Virtual Assets Red Flags; FIC Directive 9
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.10, 'Red Flag Indicators Related to Anonymity'; Directive 9, para 8.2

rules.name: Fan-in / fan-out accumulation to a single account
rules.text: Frequent transfers are made to the same VA account within a set period by more than one person or from the same IP address, or funds accumulate from many small, unrelated wallets before being consolidated and moved on.
rules.trigger: Repeated transfers to one account from multiple senders/IPs within a time window; or fan-in accumulation followed by consolidation.
capability_primitives: CP-12: AI-orchestrated layering across synthetic wallets (gap)

rules.name: Credentials or identifiers shared with another account
rules.text: A customer provides identification or account credentials (e.g. a non-standard IP address, or flash cookies) shared by another account.
rules.trigger: Identification or account credentials shared with another account.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.12, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'

rules.name: Incomplete or insufficient KYC information
rules.text: Incomplete or insufficient KYC information, or a customer declines requests for KYC documents or inquiries regarding source of funds.
rules.trigger: Customer provides incomplete KYC, or declines requests for documents or source-of-funds inquiry.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.12, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'
capability_primitives: CP-05: Coached mule/victim unable to complete CDD

rules.name: Sender or recipient lacks knowledge of the transaction
rules.text: Sender or recipient lacking knowledge or providing inaccurate information about the transaction, the source of funds, or the relationship with the counterparty.
rules.trigger: Customer cannot explain the transaction, source of funds, or counterparty relationship.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.12, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'

rules.name: Forged or edited identification documents
rules.text: Customer has provided forged documents or has edited photographs and/or identification documents as part of the on-boarding process.
rules.trigger: Customer presents forged or edited identification documents during onboarding.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.12, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'

rules.name: VA address appears on public forums linked to illegal activity
rules.text: A customer's VA address appears on public forums associated with illegal activity.
rules.trigger: Customer VA address appears on forums associated with illegal activity.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.13, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'

rules.name: Customer known to law enforcement for criminal association
rules.text: A customer is known via publicly available information to law enforcement due to previous criminal association.
rules.trigger: Customer is publicly known to law enforcement for prior criminal association.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.13, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'

rules.name: Sender unfamiliar with VA technology or custodial wallets
rules.text: Sender does not appear to be familiar with VA technology or online custodial wallet solutions.
rules.trigger: Customer demonstrates unfamiliarity with VA/custodial wallet technology.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.14, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'
capability_primitives: CP-05: Crypto-naive target of AI scam ops

rules.name: Frequent changes to identification information
rules.text: A customer frequently changes his or her identification information, including email addresses, IP addresses, or financial information. May indicate account takeover against a customer.
rules.trigger: Frequent changes to email, IP, or financial information; possible account takeover.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.14, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'

rules.name: Language in message fields indicating illicit activity
rules.text: Use of language in VA message fields indicative of the transactions being conducted in support of illicit activity or in the purchase of illicit goods, such as drugs or stolen credit card information.
rules.trigger: Message-field language indicates support of illicit activity or purchases.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.14, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'

rules.name: Repeated transactions with a subset of individuals
rules.text: A customer repeatedly conducts transactions with a subset of individuals at significant profit or loss trade, or an ML scheme to obfuscate funds flow within VASP infrastructure.
rules.trigger: Customers repeatedly transact with a subset of individuals in a clustering/trading pattern.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.14, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'

rules.name: Transactions with addresses connected to criminal schemes
rules.text: Transacting with VA addresses or bank cards connected to known fraud, extortion, or ransomware schemes, sanctioned addresses, darknet marketplaces, or other illicit websites.
rules.trigger: Counterparty VA address/card linked to fraud, extortion, ransomware, sanctions, or darknet.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.15, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'

rules.name: Crypto-to-plastic conversion or cash-funded credit cards
rules.text: The use of one or multiple credit and/or debit cards linked to a VA wallet to withdraw large amounts of fiat currency (crypto-to-plastic), or funds for purchasing VAs are sourced from cash deposits into credit cards.
rules.trigger: Large crypto-to-plastic withdrawals, or VA purchases funded from cash-deposited cards.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.15, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'

rules.name: Funds sourced from mixing services or tumbler wallets
rules.text: A customer's funds are sourced directly from third-party mixing services or wallet tumblers.
rules.trigger: Inbound funds originate from a known mixing service or tumbler.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.15, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'

rules.name: Transfers to/from an exchange not registered in the jurisdiction
rules.text: Customer's funds originate from, or are sent to, an exchange that is not registered in the jurisdiction where either the customer or exchange is located.
rules.trigger: Counterparty is an unregistered or unlicensed exchange.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.17, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'

rules.name: Offices in unregulated or no-rationale jurisdictions
rules.text: Customer sets up offices in or moves offices to jurisdictions that have no regulation or have not implemented regulations governing VAs, or sets up new offices in jurisdictions where there is no clear business rationale to do so.
rules.trigger: Customer presence in unregulated jurisdictions or offices lacking business rationale.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.17, 'Red Flag Indicators about Senders or Recipients'

rules.name: Sanctions / targeted financial sanctions screening
rules.text: The CASP must screen each customer/prospective customer against the applicable UN Security Council targeted-financial-sanctions list at onboarding and on an ongoing basis as the list updates; on a confirmed match, freeze the customer's assets, cease business with them, and file the required report with the FIC.
rules.trigger: Customer/counterparty name or identifier matches an entry on the applicable UNSC sanctions list.
capability_primitives: CP-03: Synthetic identity to dodge a real sanctioned-name match
CP-08: Identity reuse to slip back past screening

rules.name: Ongoing monitoring of high-risk PEP relationships
rules.text: A CASP must apply enhanced due diligence and ongoing monitoring to business relationships with politically exposed persons, and flag transactions inconsistent with the PEP's known or expected business or profile.
rules.trigger: PEP relationship present and transaction inconsistent with the expected profile.
capability_primitives: CP-09: AI-assisted profiling of high-value targets

rules.name: Rapid pass-through / layering through multiple hops
rules.text: A relatively small amount of value is passed through multiple VA addresses or accounts in rapid succession, consistent with layering to break the audit trail.
rules.trigger: Value passes through several hops/accounts within a short window, with little economic rationale.

rules.name: Use of anonymity-enhancing technologies (VPN/Tor)
rules.text: A customer uses anonymity-enhancing technologies such as VPNs, Tor, or IP-geolocation mismatches that obscure the origin of transactions or the customer's true location.
rules.trigger: VPN/Tor usage or IP-geolocation mismatch detected on the account or transactions.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.10, 'Red Flag Indicators Related to Anonymity'
capability_primitives: CP-06: Anonymisation tooling to obscure attribution

rules.name: Fresh wallet created immediately before first flow
rules.text: A wallet is created immediately before the first flow of funds and exhibits little or no transactional history, consistent with mule recruitment or one-time-use obfuscation.
rules.trigger: Wallet age very short (days) before its first material transaction.

rules.name: Non-hosted / self-custody wallet with attribution risk
rules.text: A transaction involves a non-hosted or self-custody wallet that complicates attribution of beneficial ownership, especially where the counterparty is high-risk.
rules.trigger: Transfer involves an unhosted/self-custody wallet.
rules.source_ref: FATF 2020, p.10, 'Red Flag Indicators Related to Anonymity'

rules.name: Source of funds inconsistent with declared wealth
rules.text: The source of funds or wealth used for VA purchases is inconsistent with the customer's apparent financial profile or declared occupation/income.
rules.trigger: Funds/wealth inconsistent with the customer's declared profile or known legitimate sources.

rules.name: Rapid accumulation then off-boarding of value
rules.text: An account rapidly accumulates value shortly after onboarding and then off-boards or withdraws nearly the entire balance, with no sustained legitimate activity.
rules.trigger: New account rapidly accumulates then withdraws near-total balance.

rules.name: Frequent or unusual source-of-funds changes
rules.text: A customer frequently changes the stated source of funds or the payment channels used to fund purchases, contrary to an established legitimate pattern.
rules.trigger: Repeated or atypical changes to funding source/channels.

rules.name: High-velocity transfer clustering in a short window
rules.text: Multiple high-value or high-velocity transfers are made in a short window, diverging from the customer's historical behaviour.
rules.trigger: Transaction velocity or value spikes far above the customer's baseline.

rules.name: Transfer to address associated with a mix of criminal indicators
rules.text: A transfer is made to an address associated with a combination of criminal indicators such as darknet markets, ransomware, scams, or other sanctioned activity.
rules.trigger: Counterparty address flagged on multiple threat-intelligence risk lists.

rules.name: Intermediate (tier-2) tokens or convertible currencies
rules.text: Transfers involve intermediate tokens, privacy coins, or directly-convertible currencies used to obscure the economic substance of the transaction.
rules.trigger: Use of privacy coins or rapid token-swapping to obscure the trail.

rules.name: Unwillingness to provide required documentation
rules.text: A customer is unwilling or evasive in providing the documentation or information required under CDD obligations.
rules.trigger: Customer evasive or unwilling to supply required CDD documentation.

rules.name: Cross-border transfer with missing originator info
rules.text: A cross-border crypto-asset transfer lacks complete originator or beneficiary identifying information that should have been transmitted under the Travel Rule.
rules.trigger: Cross-border transfer with missing or incomplete originator/beneficiary info.

rules.name: Suspicious-beneficiary VA wallet with little history
rules.text: A beneficiary VA wallet has limited transaction history yet receives transfers that are inconsistent with its apparent profile.
rules.trigger: Beneficiary wallet has little history but receives material transfers.

rules.name: Effective beneficial ownership not established
rules.text: A CASP must identify and verify the beneficial owner of any legal person or arrangement customer before establishing a business relationship, and must not proceed where ownership cannot be established.
rules.trigger: Beneficial ownership of the customer cannot be identified or verified.

rules.name: High-risk jurisdiction exposure with weak monitoring
rules.text: A customer or counterparty has material exposure to a jurisdiction identified as high-risk or with weak AML/CFT controls, without commensurate enhanced due diligence.
rules.trigger: Counterparty or fund flows to/from a high-risk or weakly regulated jurisdiction.

rules.name: Round or structured amounts with no rationale
rules.text: Transactions are conducted in round or structured amounts, or are split to avoid thresholds, with no apparent legitimate commercial rationale.
rules.trigger: Round-number or threshold-splitting transfers without economic rationale.

rules.name: AI-orchestrated synthetic-identity impersonation at onboarding
rules.text: Deepfake liveness-bypass, synthetic identity documents, and impersonation techniques are combined to pass KYC at onboarding and establish fraudulent accounts.
rules.trigger: AI-generated identity/persona signals detected at onboarding (deepfake, synthetic doc, impersonation).
rules.source: FATF (2020); ATLAS AML case studies AML.CS0033-34

rules.name: Coached mule / scam-victim behaviour pattern
rules.text: A customer exhibits behaviour consistent with a coached money mule or scam victim: limited crypto literacy, repeated transactions with a small set of wallets, and external communication with the counterparty.
rules.trigger: Crypto-naive customer repeatedly transacts with a small set of wallets consistent with mule ops.
